spots.name: Arizona State Capitol

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Arizona State Capitol is the seat of government for the U.S. state of Arizona and is located in its capital city of Phoenix.

spots.name: St. Mary's Basilica

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basilica of the Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary, also known as St. Mary's Basilica, is a Roman Catholic basilica located in Phoenix, Arizona. It was previously known as St. Mary's Church.

spots.name: Phoenix City Hall

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Phoenix City Hall is the center of government for the city of Phoenix, Arizona, United States.

spots.name: 100 West Washington

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: 100 West Washington is a high-rise skyscraper in Downtown Phoenix, Arizona, United States. It is currently the headquarters of the Phoenix Police Department.

spots.name: Chase Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Chase Tower is a 40-story skyscraper at 201 North Central Avenue in Phoenix, Arizona. Opened in 1972, the building was designed by architects Welton Becket and Fred M. Guirey. The skyscraper is located in Central Avenue Corridor, an economic and residential region of Downtown Phoenix.

spots.name: Maricopa County Courthouse
spots.summary: The Maricopa County Courthouse and Old Phoenix City Hall, also known as the County-City Administration Building, is a historic structure in downtown Phoenix, Arizona. The structure consists of two buildings in a conjoined layout sharing the same architecture.

spots.name: Renaissance Square

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Renaissance Square is a high-rise complex located in downtown Phoenix, Arizona. The complex includes two towers: One Renaissance Square at 347 ft (106 m) with 26 floors, and Two Renaissance Square at 372 ft (113 m) with 28 floors.

spots.name: Phoenix Art Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Phoenix Art Museum is the largest museum for visual art in the southwest United States. Located in Phoenix, Arizona, the museum is 285,000 square feet (26,500 m2).

spots.name: Arizona Financial Theatre
spots.summary: The Arizona Financial Theatre is a multi-use theatre in Downtown Phoenix, Arizona. The venue seats 5,000 people.

spots.name: Phoenix Police Museum

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Phoenix Police Museum is located on 2nd Avenue and Jefferson Street, on the 1st floor of the Historic Phoenix City Hall. The museum highlights the history of the Phoenix Police Department from 1881, when Henry Garfias, was elected the first city marshal to the present.

spots.name: Wells Fargo Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Wells Fargo Museum in Phoenix was one of eleven museums throughout the United States of the Wells Fargo Bank. The other museums were located in Alaska, Charlotte, Des Moines, Los Angeles, Minneapolis, Philadelphia, Portland, Sacramento, San Diego and San Francisco.

spots.name: Arizona State University Downtown Phoenix campus
spots.summary: Arizona State University Downtown Phoenix campus is one of four campuses of Arizona State University, located in Phoenix, Arizona, United States.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Arizona State University Downtown Phoenix campus

spots.name: Phoenix Symphony Hall
spots.summary: Symphony Hall is a multi-purpose performing arts venue, located at 75 North 2nd Street between North 3rd Street and East Washington Street in downtown Phoenix, Arizona. Part of Phoenix Civic Plaza, the hall is bounded to the north by the West Building of the Phoenix Convention Center.

spots.name: Rosson House

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed

spots.summary: Rosson House, at 113 North 6th Street at the corner of Monroe Street in Downtown Phoenix, Arizona, is a historic house museum in Heritage Square. It was built between 1894 and 1895 in the Stick-Eastlake - Queen Anne Style of Victorian architecture and was designed by San Francisco architect A. P.

spots.name: Wesley Bolin Memorial Plaza
spots.summary: The Wesley Bolin Memorial Plaza is an urban park and gathering place in front of the Arizona state capitol complex in downtown Phoenix, Arizona. One of the Phoenix Points of Pride, it is the site of various memorials honoring prominent figures, wars, and events in Arizona history.

spots.name: The Van Buren
spots.summary: The Van Buren is a music venue located in Downtown Phoenix, Arizona. The venue sits on the southwest corner of Van Buren St. and 4th Ave. Originally known as the Phoenix Motor Company building and the Dud R. Day Motor Company building, it was built in 1929 for the Phoenix Motor Company.

spots.name: Freeport-McMoRan Center

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Freeport-McMoRan Center is a highrise located in Downtown Phoenix, Arizona. It is located adjacent to Arizona State University's Downtown campus. Upon completion in 2009, the building was the first high-rise office tower to open in Downtown Phoenix in nearly eight years.

spots.name: United States Post Office
spots.summary: The U.S. Post Office at 522 North Central Avenue at 1st Avenue and West Fillmore Street in Phoenix, Arizona, also known as the Federal Building-U.S. Post Office, is a building of the United States federal government that was built in 1932-1936 and designed by Lescher and Mahoney in the Spanish Colonial Revival style.

spots.name: Heard Building
spots.summary: The Heard Building is a 7-story high-rise building in Phoenix, Arizona, United States, it housed the offices of The Arizona Republic and the Phoenix Gazette from 1920 to 1948. The building was constructed between 1919 and 1920 and was the first high-rise building to be erected in Phoenix.

spots.name: Bank of America Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Bank of America Tower is a highrise in downtown Phoenix, Arizona. The tower is the centerpiece of the Collier Center, a multi-use office and entertainment complex. The tower was completed in 2000 and serves as the state headquarters for Bank of America, which moved from 101 North 1st Avenue.

spots.name: Security Building
spots.summary: The Security Building is a building in downtown Phoenix, Arizona, completed in 1928 and listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1985.

spots.name: Pueblo Grande Ruin and Irrigation Sites

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: S'edav Va'aki is a pre-Columbian archaeological site and National Historic Landmark located in Phoenix, Arizona. It includes a prehistoric platform mound and irrigation canals. The City of Phoenix manages these resources through the adjacent S'edav Va'aki Museum.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Pueblo Grande Ruin and Irrigation Sites

spots.name: Celebrity Theatre
spots.summary: Celebrity Theatre is a theater in the round located in Phoenix, Arizona.

spots.name: 44 Monroe

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: 44 Monroe is a US$70 million, 523,619-square-foot (48,645.8 m2) residential high-rise building, located at the northeast corner of Monroe Street and First Avenue in Downtown Phoenix, Arizona. The 34-story tower is currently Arizona's tallest residential structure.

spots.name: Arizona Science Center

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Arizona Science Center, at 600 Washington St in Downtown Phoenix, Arizona, is a science museum located in Heritage and Science Park. It was founded in 1984 as the Arizona Museum of Science & Technology in a downtown storefront. Its current building, designed by Antoine Predock, was completed in 1997.

spots.name: Trinity Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Trinity Cathedral is an Episcopal cathedral located at 100 West Roosevelt Street in Phoenix, Arizona, in the historic Roosevelt district.

spots.name: Phoenix Trolley Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Phoenix Trolley Museum, incorporated as the Arizona Street Railway Museum, is a railway museum established in 1975, with an emphasis on preserving historical street cars in Phoenix, Arizona, US.

spots.name: Encanto Park
spots.summary: Encanto Park is a 222 acres (90 ha) public park in central Phoenix, Arizona consisting of picnic areas, a lagoon for fishing, a boat house, swimming pool, nature trail, miniature amusement park, and two golf courses. The lagoon is approximately 7.5 acres (0.030 km2) in and approximately 6 feet (1.8 m) deep.

spots.name: Phoenix Theatre
spots.summary: The Phoenix Theatre Company is a professional theatre company located in Phoenix, Arizona. Started in 1920 by a theatre troupe known as the Phoenix Players, the theatre is among the oldest continually operating theaters west of the Mississippi River.

spots.name: Arizona Mining and Mineral Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Arizona Mining and Mineral Museum in Phoenix, Arizona, was a museum focused on minerals and mining. Last operated by the Arizona Historical Society, a state government agency, its exhibits included more than 3,000 minerals, rocks, fossils, and artifacts related to the mining industry. The museum closed in May 2011.

spots.name: Monroe School

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Monroe School is a historic former school at 215 North 7th Street at the intersection of Monroe Street in downtown Phoenix, Arizona. It was designed by Norman Foote Marsh in the Neoclassical or Classical Revival style and was an elementary school and then a high school from 1914 to 1972.

spots.name: Burton Barr Central Library
spots.summary: The Burton Barr Central Library is the central library of Phoenix, Arizona. It is the flagship location and administrative headquarters for the Phoenix Public Library. It was named in honor of Burton Barr, the Republican Majority Leader in the Arizona House of Representatives from 1966 to 1986.

spots.name: First Baptist Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The First Baptist Church at in Phoenix, Arizona, was built in 1929.

spots.name: Phoenix Public Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Phoenix Public Library is a municipal library system serving Phoenix, Arizona, and operated by the city of Phoenix. There are 17 branches currently in operation citywide, anchored by the flagship Burton Barr Central Library on the northern edge of downtown Phoenix.

spots.name: Phoenix Towers
spots.summary: The Phoenix Towers were designed by Ralph C. Harris and built by Del E. Webb in Modern Movement style. The buildings, completed in 1957, are located a mile and a half north of downtown Phoenix at the corner of Central Avenue and Monte Vista Road. The main building is 14 stories with four wings forming an X.

spots.name: Roosevelt Community Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Roosevelt Community Church, formerly First Church of Christ, Scientist, Phoenix, is an historic church building located at 924 North First Street, in Phoenix, Arizona. On August 10, 1993, it was added to the National Register of Historic Places.

spots.name: Knights of Pythias Building
spots.summary: The Knights of Pythias Building in Phoenix, Arizona, United States, was built in 1928. It has served as a clubhouse and as a specialty store. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1985.

spots.name: Grace Lutheran Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Grace Lutheran Church is a historic Evangelical Lutheran Church in America church at 1124 N. 3rd Street in Phoenix, Arizona, United States.

spots.name: Sun Mercantile Building
spots.summary: The Sun Mercantile Building is a warehouse building in Phoenix, Arizona designed by E.W. Bacon and constructed by Wells & Son in 1929.

spots.name: Temple Beth Israel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Congregation Beth Israel is a Reform Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at 10460 North 56th Street in Scottsdale, Arizona, in the United States. Incorporated in 1920, the congregation affiliated with the Union for Reform Judaism in 1935.

spots.name: USS Arizona Memorial at the Arizona State Capitol
spots.summary: Pay your respects to the victims of Pearl Harbor at the Arizona State Capitol's memorial to the USS Arizona. One of the two 19,585-lb (8880-kg) anchors of the Arizona is displayed.
